user_persona: An agent with a batch and a tool that takes one item: it creates a queue over the tool, pushes up to 1 000 items per call, reads stats next session, and pauses, resumes, drains or deletes the queue; the host runs the items as ordinary trigger=queue runs within the queue's concurrency and the plan's jobs_concurrent.

acceptance_criteria.description: Given `coverage_report` over 10 registered tools with rows for 7, When it returns, Then it is `Err` naming the 3 uncovered tools and `7/10`; with rows for 8 and the other 2 in `GAPS.txt` it is `Ok`; Given a `--nocapture`-format log and a `---- <test> stdout ----` log, When `ci-shard-report.sh` runs, Then `FAILED <test>` is followed by the first panic message, also in `$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY`, cut to 2 000 bytes; with no panic text the FAILED line stands alone.

Given `target/outsch` empty, partial and full, When the coverage and branch-budget tests run, Then all three verdicts match and an invalid captured row fails the latter; 30 of 50 covered, the 20 in `GAPS.txt`, is `Err`; Given the repo, Then fixtures cover `ceil(0.8 × registered)` tools, each `GAPS.txt` line has a reason, each `host.queue.*` tool has a captured fixture, and only the branch-budget test and `outcov_ac02_*.rs` call `outsch_rows(`. Depends-on: AC 1, AC 3-7

Given a queue with `concurrency: 2` and 10 pushed items whose consumer sleeps 2 s, When `stats` is polled every 200 ms for 3 s, Then `running` reaches 2 and never exceeds it, the four counts sum to 10 at every poll, and `host.runs.list {trigger: "queue"}` never shows more than 2 runs `queued` or `running`; Given `jobs_concurrent: 1`, Then at most one is `running` at any poll.

Given a paused queue and a push of 1 000 items where items 3 and 500 break the consumer's schema, When it returns, Then `accepted` is 998, `rejected` names indexes 3 and 500, and the 998 sit `pending` in push order; Given a free tenant with 2 queues, When a third `create` runs, Then `quota_exceeded` with `data.limit {name: "queues_max", value: 2}` matching `limits.plan.queues_max`, and a push past `queue_items_max` inserts nothing and names it. Depends-on: AC 3

Given two dispatcher ticks invoked concurrently over the same pending item, When both run, Then exactly one `runs` row exists for it and the item is `running` once; Given a `running` item whose run row is missing, Then the next tick returns it to `pending`. Depends-on: AC 3

Given 4 running items, When `pause` is called, Then none starts within 3 ticks and `resume` starts the next within 2 s; Given `drain` on an empty active queue, Then it is `drained` and a `push` answers `queue_not_accepting`; Given `delete` on a drained, a paused and an active queue, Then the first two vanish and the third answers `queue_active`; Given `done` items past retention, Then the prune removes them and keeps `pending` and `running` ones. Depends-on: AC 3

Given tenant B's queue name, When tenant A calls any `host.queue.*` verb that takes `name`, `create` excepted, with it, Then `queue_not_found`; Given a `consumer_tool` A never published, When `create` runs, Then `tool_not_found`; and the three new codes appear in `host.errors` (`error_registry`, `errors.json`). Depends-on: AC 3

additional.one_migration: One migration at the next free number (0141), two new tables, compat: previous; runs gains no column.
additional.no_version_bump: No version file is bumped; wm-build land bumps and tags.
additional.claim_is_one_closure: The item claim and the runs insert happen in one with_conn closure, never across two.

five_whys_trace.q: Why does a batch of 100 items stay in the agent's session?
five_whys_trace.a: The host has no container that owns N runs: runs::enqueue starts one run per call.

five_whys_trace.q: Why is the one-run-per-call shape a problem for 100 items?
five_whys_trace.a: The agent keeps 100 run ids in its own context and paces them itself under the tenant-wide jobs_concurrent.

five_whys_trace.q: Why does a python loop not fix it?
five_whys_trace.a: It hits the plan's tool-latency ceiling or job_max_s, and a chain's for_each is bounded by chain_fanout_max and is not durable or pausable.

five_whys_trace.q: Why was the batch shape never tried?
five_whys_trace.a: No recipe asks for it and no host verb offers it.

five_whys_trace.q: Why build a primitive rather than a recipe?
five_whys_trace.a: A host-side queue with counts, pacing and pause makes the batch durable, which only the host can provide.

ambiguities_resolved.question: Does an item run under the consumer tool's budget or a queue-level override?
ambiguities_resolved.resolution: The tool's own; the queue adds no override.

ambiguities_resolved.question: Which verbs does the dispatcher deliver from?
ambiguities_resolved.resolution: active and draining queues; paused and drained queues are skipped, and a paused queue still reconciles finished items.

ambiguities_resolved.question: How are the claim and the run insert kept exactly-once?
ambiguities_resolved.resolution: One transaction in one with_conn closure that updates the item (status pending, queue active or draining, both caps) and inserts the runs row, so a reconcile cannot see a running item without its run.

ambiguities_resolved.question: How does the osreach sweep reach verbs that need a tool and a queue?
ambiguities_resolved.resolution: populate seeds a consumer tool and two queues; unreached count falls to 615 (cap lowered from 616).
